root_cause.text: In bnxt_init_one() error path, bnxt_free_hwrm_resources() destroys the HWRM DMA pool before bnxt_ptp_clear() is called, causing bnxt_ptp_enable() invoked via ptp_clock_unregister() to dereference NULL bp->hwrm_dma_pool.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states: "the error path calls bnxt_free_hwrm_resources() which destroys the DMA pool and sets bp->hwrm_dma_pool to NULL. Subsequently, bnxt_ptp_clear() is called, which invokes ptp_clock_unregister() ... ptp_clock_unregister() now calls ptp_disable_all_events() ... bnxt_ptp_enable() attempts to send HWRM commands via bnxt_ptp_cfg_pin() and bnxt_ptp_cfg_event(), both of which call hwrm_req_init(). This function tries to allocate from bp->hwrm_dma_pool, causing a NULL pointer dereference." The patch fixes the ordering by moving bnxt_ptp_clear() before bnxt_free_hwrm_resources().

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement frees the HWRM DMA pool (bp->hwrm_dma_pool) before bnxt_ptp_clear() is called, leading to a NULL dereference when bnxt_ptp_enable() attempts to use the pool.
This statement is called after the HWRM DMA pool has been freed, causing bnxt_ptp_enable() (invoked via ptp_clock_unregister()) to dereference the freed pool (NULL).
